newsitem.title: GERMANY: German insurers: Ten largest fire losses this year.
newsitem.headline: German insurers: Ten largest fire losses this year.

text.p: Insurers of Duesseldorf airport have set aside 402.6 million marks to cover claims from the 11 April blaze. Of this, 356.8 million marks have been earmarked for actual fire damage and 45.9 million marks for business interruption/loss of profit.

In addition, a claim for 24.5 million marks had been registered in the catering sector, according to the property and casualty insurers' federation VdS, which reported the figures in its internal survey of the ten largest claims so far this year.

However, insiders believe that the final sum paid out in Duesseldorf will be smaller. The insurers, led by Provinzial Duesseldorf, are at present negotiating with the airport about the payout. While Provinzial is the leader in the insurance consortium covering fire risks, the business interruption cover is led by the Gerling Group, Cologne.

According to VdS, the ten largest claims between January and October 1996 have cost insurers a total of 811.4 million marks, of which 561.1 million marks went for actual fire damage and 250.4 million marks for fire loss of profit (FLOP).
The other nine largest claims this year:

- On 16 June a chemical plant belonging to Baerlocher GmbH in Lingen caught fire, causing total damage amounting to 97.0 million marks, of which 57.0 million marks was for fire damage and 40.0 million marks for FLOP. Leading insurer is HDI.

- An explosion in a pressurised tank in Gelsenkirchen on 7 June led to damage worth 50.5 million marks at Huels AG, Vestolen GmbH and Veba Oel AG. In this case the claim was only for business interruption. The consortium is led by Gerling with five million marks and HDI with 45.5 million marks.

- A fire on the premises of mattress maker I. Breckle OHG in Benningen on 21 March resulted in a claim of 48.0 million marks, of which 28.0 million marks were for fire and 20.0 million marks for FLOP. Both risks are led by Gebudeversicherung Baden-Wuerttemberg.

- Fire damage on 30 October at Ch. Emmerich GmbH & Co. KG, a machine maker in Allendorf, led to a claim of 46.0 million marks - 26.0 million marks fire damage, and 20.0 million marks FLOP. Leading insurer here is the Frankfurter Allianz.

- The Lundwiger Messingwerke (Diehl GmbH), a metal works in Hemer, suffered damage amounting to 42.7 million marks from a fire on 9 September (22.7 million marks fire, 20.0 million marks FLOP). Zuerich International leads that policy.

- Arson was the cause of a fire in the St. Vincent hospital in Limburg on 20 June, causing damage to the value of 38.0 million marks - 18.0 million marks fire and 20.0 million marks FLOP. Aachener und Muenchener Versicherung is the leader.

- The eighth largest fire - totalling 31.0 million marks - happened on 16 March at the aluminium and plastics firm Hengste & Eckardt and at Sachsenring Automobil, both of Marsberg. The fire - started by arson - caused fire damage amounting to 21.0 million marks. FLOP damage was 10.0 million marks. Leading the consortium are Westfaelische Provinzial in Muenster with 29.0 million marks, and Colonia with two million marks.

- A fire at the margarine factory of W. Rau in Neuss on 1 April cost 28.5 million marks, of which 13.5 million marks were for fire damage and 15.0 million marks for FLOP. Nordstern- Versicherung leads both risks.

- The tenth largest fire reported by VdS was a blaze at the plant of Siener Druck GmbH in Hauenstein, which put 27.1 million marks into the books, 18.1 million marks fire and 9.0 million marks FLOP. Again, Nordstern leads most of the cover, with Bayerische Landesbrandkasse heading a smaller section with 2.1 million marks.
